summary: A 'know what you own' video using Rocket Lab's (RKLB, HOLD) earnings as the prime example. Rocket Lab fell ~5% to ~$76 after reporting, sitting ~50% below May all-time highs, and he argues the reaction makes sense: this is a ~$45B company generating only ~$770M in TTM revenue, so the 62% revenue growth and $2.35B backlog matter less than what comes next — Neutron. He reiterates his long-standing thesis: without Neutron flying and scaling, the investment thesis is broken; he now expects pad delivery in Q4 2026 but a launch closer to Q1 2027, and he is not buying more at these prices. The quarter itself was solid — $234M revenue, 41.5% non-GAAP gross margin, $2.4B cash, $397M Space Force contract, record launch agreement with Space Systems Command, and the ~$8B Iridium acquisition closing mid-2027 adding ~$500M annual FCF. He contrasts RKLB with AST SpaceMobile (ASTS, AVOID): a ~$26B company with barely any revenue and no owned launch capacity, making execution risk far higher. He extends the framework to CoreWeave — huge backlog but investors must watch margins and debt/interest payments — and warns the sell discipline applies to every name: if you only bought on hype and the stock halves, you never knew what you owned.
